question: In which year the SEBI formulated the 'Insider Trading Regulations'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Insider Trading Regulations** were first formulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** in the year **1992**. These regulations aimed to curb insider trading practices, ensuring fair and transparent functioning of the securities market. 

• The regulations are officially called the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 1992**. 

• These regulations were enacted under the powers conferred by the **SEBI Act of 1992**, which gave SEBI the authority to regulate activities in the securities market. 

• Insider trading refers to the trading of securities by individuals or entities having **privileged access to non-public, material information** about the company. 

• The 1992 regulations were a significant step toward **strengthening investor protection** and ensuring market integrity by preventing the misuse of insider information. 

• These regulations have undergone several amendments over the years to incorporate evolving market dynamics, the latest being the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **About SEBI:** 
 

• The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** was established in **1988** and was given statutory powers in **1992** under the SEBI Act. 

• SEBI is responsible for **regulating the securities market**, protecting investor interests, and promoting the development of the stock market in India. 

• It oversees various market participants, including **stock exchanges, brokers, mutual funds**, and other intermediaries. 
 
 

• **Features of SEBI Insider Trading Regulations:** 
 

• The regulations define **“insider”** as a person who has access to **unpublished price-sensitive information** about securities. 

• They prohibit insiders from **trading securities** while in possession of such information. 

• Penalties under the regulations include **monetary fines and imprisonment** as per provisions of the SEBI Act. 
 
 

• **Amendments to the Regulations:** 
 

• In **2015**, SEBI introduced revised regulations under the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015**. 

• The revised regulations focused on concepts like **Chinese Walls**, which aim to restrict the flow of sensitive information within organizations. 

• They also introduced measures for **automated monitoring** and reporting of insider trading cases using technology. 
 
 

• **Global Relevance:** 
 

• Insider trading is prohibited globally, with similar regulations in countries like the **USA (under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934)** and the **UK (under the Criminal Justice Act 1993)**. 

• International bodies such as the **International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO)** also promote best practices to address insider trading globally. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **1992 SEBI Act:** 
 

• The SEBI Act of **1992** gave SEBI **statutory powers** to regulate the securities market and prevent malpractices like insider trading. 

• The act also empowered SEBI to enforce penalties and take legal actions against violators. 
 
 

• **Role of Insider Trading Regulations:** 
 

• The regulations aim to enhance **investor confidence** by ensuring transparency and fairness in trading practices. 

• They play a crucial role in maintaining the **integrity of financial markets** and safeguarding small investors from exploitation. 
 
 

• **Recent Developments:** 
 

• SEBI has introduced measures like **online reporting systems**, whistleblower mechanisms, and stricter penalties for insider trading violations. 

• It has been focusing on leveraging **technology and data analytics** to detect suspicious trading activities more efficiently.
